subject: Localization and deletion controls — VPC deployment Q&A

Subject: Data handling in our VPC - residency, backups, deletion timelines

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-up questions from Legal & Security so we can sign off on the Private/VPC deployment for Nordic Retail:

1) Residency guarantee: can you confirm all customer data (user prompts, model I/O, logs) will remain within our EU VPC and not leave region boundaries?
2) Backups & snapshots: what automated backup mechanisms exist for the deployment and where are snapshots stored? Are backups replicated cross-region by default?
3) Deletion timeline: when we ask Redwood to delete a customer (or project) dataset, what are the steps and how long until data is unrecoverable across primary storage, caches, and backups?
4) Proof of deletion: do you provide an attestation/certificate and how are deletions logged for auditing?

We need concise answers to include in the procurement package. If you prefer, we can set up a short call with our CISO.

Best,
Anna
Privacy Officer | Nordic Retail Co

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordicretail.co>
Cc: Jens Moller <jmoller@legal.nordicretail.co>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data handling in our VPC - residency, backups, deletion timelines

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching our operational playbook and SOC2 summary for the detailed bits.

Residency guarantee:
- In Private/VPC deployments, customer data is processed and stored only on nodes you control (your VPC/subnet). The control plane (management) coordinates orchestration but is configured to avoid data egress for model I/O — we will not route customer data out of your EU region without explicit written consent.

Backups & snapshots:
- By default, we create automated periodic snapshots of model-serving volumes (configurable cadence). Snapshots are stored in the same region and, for Private deployments, in your customer-controlled bucket (you specify the storage account). Cross-region replication is not enabled by default — it must be agreed and configured during onboarding.

Deletion timeline & process:
- Step 1: Admin request submitted (console/API) to mark dataset/tenant for deletion.
- Step 2: Immediate logical deletion from active storage and KV caches (within minutes).
- Step 3: Background purge job removes data from primary disks and application indexes (within 24–72 hours, depends on shard size).
- Step 4: Snapshots/backups: retention is controlled by your backup lifecycle policy. When you request full erasure, we schedule deletion of snapshots; complete removal from backup storage can take up to 30 days depending on provider retention policies.
- Step 5: Cryptographic erasure option: if you enable customer-managed keys, we can perform key revocation/rotation which renders encrypted backups unreadable immediately (recommended for fastest irrecoverability).

Proof of deletion & logging:
- All deletion operations emit auditable events to your logging endpoint (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Equivalents) and to the Redwood audit log (configurable retention). We can produce an attestation document summarizing deletion actions and timestamps; for formal requests we use DocuSign to sign off.

Attachments: deletion-playbook-v1.docx (playbook with step-by-step ops), SOC2-summary-redwood.pdf (controls overview).

If useful, Karthik can add technical details about snapshots and KMS. Otherwise happy to schedule the CISO call.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data handling in our VPC - residency, backups, deletion timelines

Anna — adding the technical clarifications you asked for. Short bullets to put in your security questionnaire: 

- Snapshots/backups: For Private deployments we rely on the storage account you nominate. Snapshots are created as point-in-time copies of volumes; they remain in your account/region. We do not enable cross-region replication unless configured.
- Cache eviction: KV caches (model context cache) are in-memory per node and flushed on logical delete. Persistent cache artifacts (if any) are tied to the serving node and removed by the purge job described by Lauren.
- Backed-up logs: Operational logs (instance diagnostics, agent logs) are streamed to your logging endpoint; retention follows your logging lifecycle. We can configure shorter retention for security-sensitive tenants.
- Encryption & KMS: You can provide a customer-managed KMS key. For deletion, Kami (our key management integration) supports key rotation/revocation which immediately renders ciphertext unusable even if snapshots remain. This is the best path to rapid irrecoverability of encrypted backups.
- Verification: We can perform post-deletion scans to verify absence of tenant data and provide a verification report; timing depends on dataset size (typical completion 3–10 business days after deletion request).

If you need exact API call examples for automated deletion, tell me and I will paste a sample.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
